name: frBTC Wrap/Unwrap Flow Tracing
summary: Trace a chain of frBTC wrap/swap/unwrap/dispatch transactions to compute net BTC flow, expected vs actual payouts, and flag undisclosed fees.
whenToUse: Use when auditing a Bitcoin address's wdsx7/frBTC/Alkanes transaction history to verify wrap fees, deferred dispatch payouts, and whether stated 'no fee' claims hold up against on-chain data.
inputs: Per-TX inputs/outputs with BTC and frBTC amounts
Any protocol fee claims to verify
outputs: Cost breakdown by category (miner fees, AMM slippage, dust, residual)

name: BTCfi Hype vs Real Rubric
summary: Classify a BTCfi claim, protocol, or narrative as Real, Hype, or Mixed using a checklist derived from BTCfi's history (trust/custody, valuation-vs-mechanism, adversarial testing, indexer fragility).
whenToUse: Use when asked whether a new Bitcoin-DeFi project, yield narrative, or 'trustless' bridge claim is substantive infrastructure or speculative froth.
inputs: Description of the BTCfi protocol/claim/narrative to evaluate
Any stated valuations, TVL, or yield figures
outputs: Answers to the four checks (trust/custody, valuation-vs-mechanism, adversarial/scale test, indexer fragility)
Verdict: Real / Hype / Mixed, with what's-real and what's-hype lines

name: Evidence-to-Pipeline Layering
summary: Structure an organization's data model into 5 traceable layers (evidence, extractions, operational facts, stage records, pipelines) so decisions stay human-controlled and traceable back to source evidence.
whenToUse: Use when designing a data model or system architecture for any evaluation/decision workflow (deal flow, hiring, sales, research triage, grant review) that needs to go from unstructured source material to structured, auditable decisions.
inputs: Existing data/artifacts the org already collects (recordings, notes, records)
The subject(s) being evaluated (single entity or combination)
Where business decisions currently get made
outputs: A layer table mapping domain artifacts to the 5 layers
Reevaluation model for stage records (freeze + new row + staleness flag)

name: Process-vs-State Modeling
summary: Design or clean up a pipeline/workflow model by strictly separating processes (activities) from states (stages a subject is in).
whenToUse: Use whenever a workflow, pipeline, or stage-based system's terminology is ambiguous or mixes activity and status into the same field.
inputs: List of terms currently used to describe workflow stages
One real subject to trace through the pipeline as a worked example
outputs: Pipeline drawn as an alternating state → process → state sequence

name: Pipeline-vs-Campaign Pattern
summary: Split a reusable process definition (pipeline) from its implemented real-world runs (campaigns) so a shared template can be instantiated repeatedly against different cohorts or initiatives.
whenToUse: Use when a team keeps redefining 'how we do X' from scratch for every new batch/cohort/initiative instead of running a shared template.
inputs: The process/workflow currently being redefined per batch or cohort
At least one other real or plausible use of the same process
outputs: A list of campaigns instantiating it
Flags for pipeline/campaign coupling found during extraction

name: Marketplace Competitor Quadrant Mapping
summary: Map a marketplace/collectibles competitive landscape by scoring competitors on bipolar dimensions, categorizing by business model, and plotting dimension pairs as quadrants to find positioning whitespace.
whenToUse: Use when asked to build a competitor map, positioning matrix, or whitespace analysis for a marketplace, RWA/tokenization, or collectibles-style product.
inputs: List of competitors and direct product research on each
Candidate scoring dimensions relevant to the category
outputs: Competitor score matrix with evidence notes
2-3 quadrant plots with one-sentence insights, one flagged primary

name: Marketplace Cross-Market Pain-Point Synthesis
summary: Synthesize region/segment-specific marketplace research into a small set of universal pain points, each annotated with its region-specific manifestation, to find a hook that works across otherwise different markets.
whenToUse: Use when turning scattered regional/segment research into a small number of evidence-backed cross-market themes for a marketplace or collectibles product.
inputs: Region/segment-specific research with sourced claims on motivation, trust, and friction
outputs: 3-5 cross-market pain points with per-region manifestations

name: Junior-vs-Senior Cost Framework
summary: Compare two hiring tiers on cost-per-unit-of-output using four levers (capacity ramp, quality/rework penalty, sustainable hours, salary relative to market) instead of comparing salary directly.
whenToUse: Use when asked whether hiring junior or senior engineers (or a similar two-tier staffing decision) is more cost-effective, or why a cheaper hire isn't necessarily cheaper per unit of output.
inputs: Assumptions for each of the four levers per tier
outputs: Net output and cost-per-output per tier
Sensitivity statement naming the dominant lever(s)
